paragraphs: Children in care in Devon are looked after by Devon County Council's own service, Fostering Devon, and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. In May 2026 the council said around 810 children were in its care but only around 271 approved foster homes were available, so some children live outside the county or in residential homes. More than 30 people were then going through assessment, and the council said many more carers are still needed.

Fostering Devon has changed how it recruits, working more closely with local communities, businesses and its existing carers. It held a Hearts and Homes conference in Exeter built around real experiences and questions rather than a sales pitch, and runs free, informal information sessions online, in person and at pop-up stalls, listed through Fostering South West. Going along does not commit you to anything.

The council has also highlighted a national shortage of carers who can keep brothers and sisters together, and says that not having two spare bedrooms need not rule you out, as some younger siblings can share a room.

To foster with the council you need to be over 21 and have a spare bedroom; you can be single or in a couple, working or retired. Agencies set their own fees and support, so speak to Fostering Devon and two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about training, out-of-hours help and what they pay, before you choose.

sources.title: New approach to recruiting foster carers in Devon showing early impact (Devon County Council, May 2026)
More foster carers who can look after siblings needed (Devon County Council)
